answer.short: $\frac{3}{4}>\frac{2}{4}$. Shade $3$ of $4$ parts in each left bar; $1$ of $2$ parts above and $2$ of $4$ parts below on the right.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}&=\frac{1\times2}{2\times2}\\&=\frac{2}{4}\end{aligned}$$
Shade the models as shown. Since $3>2$, $\frac{3}{4}>\frac{2}{4}$.

answer.short: $\frac{8}{12}<\frac{9}{12}$. Shade $2$ of $3$ and $8$ of $12$ parts on the left; $3$ of $4$ and $9$ of $12$ parts on the right.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{2\times4}{3\times4}\\&=\frac{8}{12}\\\frac{3}{4}&=\frac{3\times3}{4\times3}\\&=\frac{9}{12}\end{aligned}$$
Shade the models as shown. Since $8<9$, $\frac{8}{12}<\frac{9}{12}$.

answer.short: $\frac{4}{6}>\frac{3}{6}$. Divide each lower bar into $6$ equal parts; shade $4$ on the left and $3$ on the right. Shade $2$ of $3$ upper-left parts and $1$ of $2$ upper-right parts.
answer.worked:
The lowest common multiple of $3$ and $2$ is $6$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{2\times2}{3\times2}\\&=\frac{4}{6}\\\frac{1}{2}&=\frac{1\times3}{2\times3}\\&=\frac{3}{6}\end{aligned}$$
Divide both lower bars into six equal parts and shade the models as shown. Since $4>3$, $\frac{4}{6}>\frac{3}{6}$.
